items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: we were joined by a trombonist named Frank Orchard, and the trumpetist Jack Butler.

ctx.x: But when Barney came back, Leon told him that we had a run-in, and asked me what happened. I told him my side of the story, as I didn't know what his brother had told him. The only thing that Barney had to say is that he thought I was a little too continental. What I think he would have loved to have told me was that I had too much nerve and pride for a Negro. But everything went smoothly afterwards.

World war number two had been going on for nearly two years in America. The trio was beginning to become popular, and we co-starred with Hazel Scott after her return from Hollywood for a benefit to buy watches for the Soviet Army, which had taken place at Carnegie Hall the 11th of April, 1943. The trio did a few numbers and for the finale, we were joined by a trombonist named Frank Orchard, and the trumpetist Jack Butler.
